capability.description: Accepted product behavior is strict, reviewable, and measurable beside the implementation.
capability.name: Living product contract

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must reject repository contract documents that violate the accepted Story and Acceptance Criterion schema.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Structural failures make semantic impact and synchronization untrustworthy.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must compile deterministic manifests and report direct-AC and repository mapping coverage with explicit gaps.

scenarios.given: ten eligible source files and eight mapped paths
scenarios.then: Tieline must report 80 percent coverage and name both unmapped files
scenarios.when: mapping coverage is calculated

scenarios.given: configured source roots contain no eligible files
scenarios.then: Tieline must report that coverage is not measured instead of reporting 100 percent
scenarios.when: mapping coverage is calculated

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must report affected Acceptance Criteria and freshness for changed, renamed, or deleted linked paths without blocking on semantic findings.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Drift should be visible during review while the MVP remains warn-only.

scenarios.given: a linked implementation path changes without a refreshed manifest
scenarios.then: Tieline must report the linked criterion as impacted and stale
scenarios.when: the branch is checked against its base

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must render accepted Stories and Acceptance Criteria as a self-contained human-readable review page.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Maintainers outside the implementation can review the same repository-owned contract accepted by the pull request.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must store the compiled manifest as one file per capability beside a repository-level index, must delete the file of any capability the contract no longer declares, and must refuse to read a manifest whose file names disagree with the capabilities they hold.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: A single generated manifest made every branch that touched any specification file conflict with every other one, even when the capabilities they changed were disjoint, and let a partial line merge produce a manifest that parses but that no compilation would emit.

scenarios.given: a compiled manifest whose capability was removed from the specification
scenarios.then: Tieline must delete that capability's manifest file and leave every other file in the manifest directory untouched
scenarios.when: the contract is compiled again

scenarios.given: a manifest file whose name does not match the capability it holds
scenarios.then: Tieline must refuse the manifest and name both the file and the capability instead of accepting the capability under the wrong identity
scenarios.when: the manifest is read

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must fail the check when the committed manifest differs from the manifest the contract compiles to, unless that gate is explicitly downgraded.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: A manifest merged without recompilation records evidence hashes that were never reviewed against the code they name. Comparing the committed manifest with a fresh compilation is a byte diff of a deterministic function, so nothing is being judged, which is the same reason broken links already fail. Findings that do need judgement stay warn-only.

scenarios.given: a specification file changed without the manifest being recompiled
scenarios.then: Tieline must report the stale manifest as an error and exit non-zero
scenarios.when: the branch is checked against its base

scenarios.given: the same stale manifest and an explicit request to downgrade the gate
scenarios.then: Tieline must report the stale manifest as a warning and exit zero
scenarios.when: the branch is checked against its base

scenarios.given: a manifest that cannot be recompiled at all
scenarios.then: Tieline must report the compilation failure once rather than also reporting it as a stale manifest
scenarios.when: the branch is checked against its base

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must require every contract link to state whether its claim was authored, inferred, or materialized, and must preserve that provenance through compiled manifests, repository synchronization, and every exact claim read.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Relation and target describe what a link claims, while provenance records how that claim entered its current authority surface. Keeping this low-cardinality origin distinct from freshness and grade lets agents interpret a claim without turning mutable review facts into contract identity.

scenarios.given: a contract link has no provenance
scenarios.then: Tieline must reject the link instead of guessing where its claim came from
scenarios.when: the repository contract is validated

scenarios.given: only a contract link's provenance changes
scenarios.then: Tieline must change the owning contract hash without creating a second link identity
scenarios.when: the contract manifest is compiled

scenarios.given: an accepted repository link was copied during planning-to-repository authority transfer
scenarios.then: Tieline must preserve materialized as the origin of that exact claim
scenarios.when: the repository contract is synchronized and read

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must keep the compiled manifest independent of Git revision, identify exact manifest reads with a content-derived digest, and supply Git commit provenance explicitly only when synchronizing the reviewed manifest to the database.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: A revision in the tracked repository-level index made every branch conflict in one shared generated file and became stale as soon as that generated file was committed. Content identity belongs to the reviewed manifest, while Git revision belongs to the runtime projection checkpoint and audit boundary.

scenarios.given: accepted specifications and linked artifacts whose content is unchanged across two Git revisions
scenarios.then: the repository-level manifest index must remain byte-identical and must not record either Git revision
scenarios.when: the contract is compiled at each revision

scenarios.given: the content of the reviewed manifest changes
scenarios.then: Tieline must return a different manifest digest identifying the complete reviewed manifest that answered
scenarios.when: exact path criteria are requested

scenarios.given: a reviewed manifest and an explicit runtime Git commit
scenarios.then: Tieline must use that runtime commit for projection rows, checkpoint guards, sync results, and audit events without adding it to the reviewed manifest
scenarios.when: the repository contract is synchronized

stories.benefit: intent and implementation change through the same review
stories.goal: define product behavior in a stable Story and Acceptance Criterion hierarchy
stories.title: Review accepted behavior with code

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must report every acceptance criterion linked to an exact repository-relative path, must distinguish a link carried by the acceptance criterion itself from one carried only by its Story, and must return an explicit has_criteria, no_criteria, or not_found status for every requested path.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Coverage answers for the whole contract and check answers for a diff, so both describe a violation that already exists; the pre-change question is the only one that can prevent it. An empty array reads to an agent like a failed query rather than the actionable finding that an existing path has no recorded acceptance criteria.

scenarios.given: a path is linked by one acceptance criterion and by the Story that owns it
scenarios.then: Tieline must return has_criteria with both records marked direct and story_fallback
scenarios.when: the contract criteria for that path are requested

scenarios.given: a path exists in the repository and no contract link targets it
scenarios.then: Tieline must return no_criteria and state that no acceptance criteria apply instead of returning an empty result
scenarios.when: the contract criteria for that path are requested

scenarios.given: a requested path does not exist in the repository
scenarios.then: Tieline must return not_found distinctly from an existing path with no criteria
scenarios.when: the contract criteria for that path are requested

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The path-criteria lookup must answer from the compiled manifest alone, so Tieline must serve get_path_criteria over MCP with no database connection and must return a named, actionable message when no workspace or no readable manifest is found.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Every other MCP tool fails at call time without Postgres, so an offline server boots and answers nothing; a manifest-backed lookup is what makes serving without a database worth doing, and an obscure throw would waste the one answer the caller came for.

scenarios.given: no database connection is configured
scenarios.then: Tieline must return the applicable acceptance criteria and the content-derived digest of the manifest that answered
scenarios.when: the contract criteria for a path are requested over MCP

scenarios.given: the server runs outside any Tieline workspace
scenarios.then: Tieline must name the missing workspace and the command that creates one
scenarios.when: the contract criteria for a path are requested

aliases: which acceptance criteria apply to this file
stories.benefit: a contradiction with accepted behavior is prevented instead of reported afterwards
stories.goal: resolve a repository path to the acceptance criteria already recorded for it
stories.title: Learn which acceptance criteria apply to a path before editing it

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given an exact repository-relative code or test path with optional kind and selector, Tieline must preserve the complete locator identity, return has_context, no_criteria, or not_found explicitly, include exact-selector and file-level claims while excluding other selectors, and bound associated assets to one Acceptance-Criterion-mediated intent neighborhood.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: A known symbol should retrieve the reviewed behavior that applies to that symbol without collapsing same-file claims or pretending the result is an open-ended graph traversal.

scenarios.given: one file has claims for function:first, function:second, and the whole file
scenarios.then: Tieline must return the function:first and file-level claims with their kind, repository, canonical path, selector, framework hint, relation, provenance, and link scope while excluding function:second
scenarios.when: exact asset context is requested for function:first

scenarios.given: an existing path has no applicable claim for the requested selector
scenarios.then: Tieline must return no_criteria distinctly from not_found for a missing path
scenarios.when: exact asset context is requested

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given an exact Acceptance Criterion stable ID, Tieline must return its Capability and Story ancestry, lifecycle, criterion, rationale, applicability, scenarios, direct links, Story-fallback links, and directly associated code and test assets without recursive code-to-code traversal.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Reviewers need the accepted product record and its bounded contract coupling, not a semantic approximation or an inferred runtime dependency graph.

scenarios.given: an Acceptance Criterion has a direct test link and inherits a Story-level implementation link
scenarios.then: Tieline must preserve both assets, their direct or story_fallback scope, and the owning product context in deterministic order
scenarios.when: its exact context is requested

scenarios.given: the stable ID does not identify an accepted Acceptance Criterion
scenarios.then: Tieline must return an explicit not_found status and an actionable answer naming the unknown stable ID and reviewed manifest
scenarios.when: exact context is requested

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Every code or test claim returned as exact intent context must keep provenance, link scope, content freshness, locator resolution, and semantic support as separate assurance dimensions, must preserve broken and uninspectable claims with honest causes or unknown states, and must report semantic support as not_assessed.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Structural currency and selector resolution can guide review, but neither proves the linked behavior or records that a linked test executed or passed.

scenarios.given: a current local implementation selector resolves against its reviewed content
scenarios.then: provenance, freshness, and locator resolution must be positive while semantic support remains not_assessed
scenarios.when: exact intent context is returned

scenarios.given: a local target is missing or a selector uses an unsupported language
scenarios.then: the claim must remain visible with a named broken cause or not_checked state and must not be converted into semantic failure
scenarios.when: its claim is inspected

scenarios.given: an associated target names another repository
scenarios.then: freshness and locator resolution must remain honestly unknown or not_checked
scenarios.when: its claim is inspected from this checkout

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must expose separate get_asset_intent_context and get_acceptance_criterion_context MCP tools and equivalent contract context --path and --ac CLI modes that answer from the compiled manifest without a database and preserve the same membership, statuses, repository key, and content-derived manifest digest.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Agents need primitive exact reads while maintainers need CLI and JSON parity to inspect the same reviewed contract and actionable workspace or manifest failures.

scenarios.given: no database, embeddings, network, or knowledge store is configured and the compiled manifest is readable
scenarios.then: both surfaces must return the same bounded neighborhood membership and manifest identity
scenarios.when: equivalent exact context requests are made over MCP and CLI

scenarios.given: no workspace or no readable manifest is available
scenarios.then: Tieline must return a named actionable result that explains how to initialize or compile the workspace
scenarios.when: either MCP exact context tool is called

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Diff impact must preserve selector-qualified target identity and report resolved, unresolved, or not_checked locator state for affected links while keeping selector findings advisory and describing shared Acceptance-Criterion links only as contract coupling rather than runtime dependency or comprehensive blast radius.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Selector drift is useful review input, but conservative inspection cannot establish execution topology and must not create a new blocking gate.

scenarios.given: a changed file contains one unresolved selector claim and one selector in an unsupported source language
scenarios.then: both claims must remain distinct with unresolved and not_checked locator states and selector findings must not change the existing exit behavior
scenarios.when: diff impact is calculated

stories.benefit: implementation and review begin from bounded accepted intent with honest current assurance
stories.goal: retrieve the exact reviewed context for a known code or test locator or Acceptance Criterion
stories.title: Inspect precise accepted intent before changing an asset
